newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine teachers call strike for June 20.
newsitem.headline: Argentine teachers call strike for June 20.

text.p: Argentina's teachers have called a 24 hour strike for June 20 to increase pressure on the government to raise their salaries, a union official said Wednesday.
Small groups of teachers across the country have been on hunger strike for 70 days in protest at their pay.
The teachers want their minimum wage to be raised to $500 from the current monthly pay of around $300.
"We will continue the hunger strike in all provinces, together with a national march June 20," Cleila Levini, union secretary at the Argentine Education Workers Confederation, told Reuters.
Argentina has an unemployment rate of 17.3 percent, and has recently been hit by a wave of roadblocks and protests against poverty and joblessness in its provinces.
A report Wednesday said two-fifths of Argentina's salary-earners are paid less than $500 a month, according to a government study published in the Clarin newspaper Wednesday.
